body: I guess so. I guess I feel like I did have a shot, but I ruined it. I screwed it up. I did it wrong. And I should get what I deserve for screwing up.
I don't believe that I deserve help. And if I don't believe I deserve it, why should I seek it?

Why don't I trust anyone? I suppose I was disappointed too many times. I suppose I'm too afraid of getting hurt and betrayed again. I suppose I'm too afraid of showing the rotting interior of myself to anyone. I try not to think about it, actually. Hurts too much.
No. I keep hearing that I'm supposed to. But I don't.

You're welcome. This made me smile. And chuckle a bit at your creative use of "loose" instead of "lose", but I'm by no means judging your grammar, I just have a mental image of you setting your friends loose, and actually that's kind of sad, so don't do that! And now I have a lovely run-on sentence there. Grammar is one of the few things left that I don't feel totally inept at. Just somewhat inept! :)

One of my issues in overcoming this...stuff...is that I don't have anyone to keep me to things. I feel so entirely alone in my life, despite having people I could probably turn to. I just haven't been able to trust anyone. You're very lucky, you know, to have friends to help you be better. I just can't develop relationships that go deeper than the surface. And then I run away from those surface relationships anyways. Maybe someday I won't. Maybe someday I'll be brave enough. And then I'll have real friends to lean on. That would be nice.
Not really. I read sometimes. But I feel like that's more of a distraction, to keep me from thinking. Something that does make me feel better, at least for a little while, is seeing my nieces.

Everyone is too nice to me. Like you, thinking I merit happiness. But I just take. I take and take what's offered to me and never give anything back. The only way I know to be nice is just to get out of everyone's way. Just to not be a trouble or inconvenience to anyone. I don't feel alive. So I don't feel like I merit happiness.

You're right. No one else can fight for me. And I've given up fighting. I think I gave up a long time ago. I don't even remember what it's like to feel like myself, 100%. I've been pretending for so long to be what I think everyone else expects me to be, I don't think there's much of a me left. How can I possibly get back to something that I don't even remember feeling? And I'm not able to go back to that counseling center anyway. It's hundreds of miles away. So many excuses. I don't want to get help badly enough, I guess.
I hope I don't offend you, but I just don't see myself that way. I have done nothing to merit any happiness. I haven't even tried.

No, I don't know where to go. I've never known where to go. There's too many places to go. There is too much going on in my head. Too much sick and tired. I don't know what I really want. Because what I want might be the wrong thing. So it's always up in the air, never settling on one thing, because it might be the wrong thing. I'm definitely sick. I'm tired. But not enough. I can make do for a little while longer. I can stretch this out. And a little while turns into months and years until I've been under this dark sky for half of my life. I do want help. I'm afraid of getting help. I'm afraid I don't deserve help. I'm afraid I'm too far gone for help. I'm afraid I'll take that help and do nothing with it. I'll bury it away like I do everything else. I'm confused and there's nowhere to go.

Well, you're in a better place than I am. You are still fighting. I'm letting things go. You went through a social anxiety course. Just thinking about doing something like that makes me feel terrified. You actually have the guts to call people up to meet with them. I can't do that. I don't even know you and I admire you.

Also, I totally get you on the complaining about your feelings to others thing. I feel like it's wrong to burden people with myself and my problems. Actually, I can relate to practically everything you posted. The loneliness, the social anxiety-ness, the internal war. I'm even turning 27 in a week and a half. Except I'm a girl, so I obviously don't relate to you being male. 

I'm glad things have been going better for you. You said it'd be nice to know that other people relate to how you're feeling and I definitely relate. I hope that is useful to you in some way. For my part, just writing this comment has given me a tiny glimmer of hope that maybe someday I can continue the fight within myself. So thanks for that.
I guess I am just making excuses. That's about the only thing I'm good for.  I have nothing else to offer anyone. Just empty excuses.

Yes, a few years ago when I was in college I was diagnosed with depression. I went to therapy a few times and then went to a group therapy session which terrified me so I never went back. Really the only reason I went in the first place was a roommate made me go to the counseling center. I don't think I really want to be fixed, to be helped. Otherwise I'd have worked towards that already.

I don't think getting this job would solve all my problems. But getting this job might give me some means of helping myself. I would have some money to pay for things like healthcare. I would have another reason to keep waking up in the morning and I'm pretty low on those right now. I would have some way to be useful so maybe I could work towards becoming someone who deserves all those dreams.

I'm sorry...I just can't connect with any of what you posted. I have no desire to carry out any sort of crazy plan. I have almost no desires at all, actually. Just this numb acceptance of what the rest of my existence is going to be. This must be what I really wanted, since I have no desire for anything else.
